ruleset.name: Sonar
ruleset.description: Implementing Sonar rules through PMD custom rules.

rule.name: ClassComparedByNameCheck
rule.message: Avoid comparing class names directly. Use 'instanceof' or 'Class.isAssignableFrom()' instead.

description.p: There is no requirement that class names be unique, only that they be unique within a package. Therefore trying to determine an object's type based on its class name is an exercise fraught with danger. One of those dangers is that a malicious user will send objects of the same name as the trusted class and thereby gain trusted access.
Instead, the instanceof operator or the Class.isAssignableFrom() method should be used to check the object's underlying type.

rule.name: RSAUsesOAEPCheck
rule.message: Cryptographic RSA algorithms should always incorporate OAEP (Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding)

description.p: Without OAEP in RSA encryption, it takes less work for an attacker to decrypt the data or infer patterns from the ciphertext. This rule logs an issue as soon as a literal value starts with RSA/NONE.

rule.example:
Cipher rsa = javax.crypto.Cipher.getInstance("RSA/NONE/NoPadding");// Noncompliant
Cipher rsa = javax.crypto.Cipher.getInstance("RSA/ECB/OAEPWITHSHA-256ANDMGF1PADDING");// Compliant

rule.name: ShiftOnIntOrLongCheck
rule.message: Ints and longs should not be shifted by zero or more than their number of bits-1

description.p: Since an int is a 32-bit variable, shifting by more than +/-31 is confusing at best and an error at worst. Shifting an int by 32 is the same as shifting it by 0, and shifting it by 33 is the same as shifting it by 1.
Similarly, shifting a long by +/-64 is the same as shifting it by 0, and shifting it by 65 is the same as shifting it by 1.

rule.name: ThreadAsRunnableArgumentCheck
rule.message: Threads should not be used where Runnables are expected

description.p: While it is technically correct to use a Thread where a Runnable is called for, the semantics of the two objects are different, and mixing them is a bad practice that will likely lead to headaches in the future.
The crux of the issue is that Thread is a larger concept than Runnable. A Runnable is an object whose running should be managed. A Thread expects to manage the running of itself or other Runnables.

rule.name: UnusedReturnedDataCheck
rule.message: read and readLine return values should be used

description.p: When a method is called that returns data read from some data source, that data should be stored rather than thrown away. Any other course of action is surely a bug.
This rule raises an issue when the return value of any of the following is ignored or merely null-checked: BufferedReader.readLine(), Reader.read(), and these methods in any child classes.
